title: Meta Clustering of Neural Bandits

problem.claim: Recommendation is formulated as a sequential contextual-bandit decision problem over T rounds, with the objective of minimizing regret.

gap.claim: Existing work is extended to arbitrary reward functions to balance user heterogeneity and user correlations in recommender systems.

contributions.claim: Introduces the Clustering of Neural Bandits problem for recommender systems with arbitrary reward functions.
Proposes M-CNB, using a meta-learner to represent and rapidly adapt to dynamic clusters together with an informative UCB-based exploration strategy.
Provides an instance-dependent performance guarantee that withstands adversarial context and is reported to be at least as good as state-of-the-art approaches under the same assumptions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the Clustering of Neural Bandits problem as new and M-CNB as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The proposed algorithm is reported to have an instance-dependent guarantee that withstands adversarial context.
In extensive experiments across recommendation and online classification scenarios, M-CNB is reported to outperform state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report improved online recommendation and online classification performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Contextual bandits provide a sequential decision-making framework for recommendation with regret minimization as the objective.
The paper studies Clustering of Neural Bandits to address arbitrary reward functions while balancing user heterogeneity and correlations.
M-CNB combines meta-learning for dynamic clusters with UCB-based exploration.
The paper gives an instance-dependent guarantee under adversarial context and compares it with state-of-the-art guarantees under matched assumptions.
Experiments in recommendation and online classification report that M-CNB outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method combines a representation mechanism for dynamic clusters with an exploration strategy tailored to uncertainty.

interpretation.claim: Separating adaptation to changing structure from exploration may help address both nonstationary user groups and decision uncertainty.

application.claim: Online recommendation or classification systems with evolving user or task clusters could consider combining adaptive clustering with confidence-based exploration.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination remains effective outside the stated settings or assumptions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact arbitrary reward-function class or clustering assumptions.
The abstract does not report the quantitative form of the performance guarantee or regret bounds.
The abstract does not identify datasets, baseline implementations, or experimental results.
The abstract does not provide reproducibility details.
